concepts.name: Copy's single action goal
concepts.summary: Explain that copy exists to move a reader toward one specific action such as clicking, buying or signing up, not just to inform or entertain.

concepts.name: Target reader identification
concepts.summary: Describe who the copy is for and what that reader wants, fears and already knows.

concepts.name: Features versus benefits
concepts.summary: Distinguish what a product has (feature) from what it does for the reader (benefit) and recognise which a line states.

concepts.name: Headline's role
concepts.summary: Recall that the headline must earn attention and promise something that makes the reader continue.

concepts.name: Call to action basics
concepts.summary: Identify a call to action as the explicit instruction telling the reader what to do next.

concepts.name: Clear plain-language writing
concepts.summary: Understand why short sentences, concrete words and the reader's own vocabulary beat jargon and vague claims.

concepts.name: Copy formats and channels
aliases: ad, email, landing page, product page
concepts.summary: Name the main copy formats (ads, landing pages, emails, product pages) and what each is typically used for.

misconceptions.text: Good copy is mainly clever, creative wording that shows off the writer's style.
Listing everything the product can do is the same as persuading the reader.
A call to action is optional if the text is good enough.

concepts.name: Turning features into benefits
concepts.summary: Convert a feature list into reader-focused benefits by repeatedly asking 'so what?' until an outcome the reader values appears.

concepts.name: Headline formulas
concepts.summary: Write headlines using proven patterns such as benefit, how-to, number, question and curiosity, and choose one that fits the goal.

concepts.name: You-focused voice
concepts.summary: Rewrite company-centred sentences ('we offer') into reader-centred ones ('you get') without losing accuracy.

concepts.name: Writing effective CTAs
concepts.summary: Write specific, action-and-outcome CTAs such as 'Get my free guide' in place of generic ones like 'Submit'.

concepts.name: Scannable layout
concepts.summary: Structure copy with subheads, short paragraphs and bullets so a skimming reader grasps the offer.

concepts.name: Social proof elements
concepts.summary: Explain how testimonials, ratings and usage figures reduce doubt and apply them in appropriate places.

concepts.name: Email subject lines
concepts.summary: Write subject lines that are clear, relevant and honest enough to earn an open and match the email's content.

misconceptions.text: A benefit is just a feature described with more enthusiastic adjectives.
The more curiosity a headline creates, the better, even if it hides what the page offers.
Readers read all the copy carefully, so formatting does not matter.

concepts.name: Audience research and voice-of-customer
concepts.summary: Analyse reviews, interviews and support tickets to extract the pains, desires and exact phrases customers use, and build copy from them.

concepts.name: Awareness-level matching
concepts.summary: Diagnose how aware a reader is of the problem and solution and choose the opening angle accordingly.

concepts.name: Persuasion structures
concepts.summary: Apply frameworks such as AIDA and Problem-Agitate-Solve to organise copy and judge when each suits the goal.

concepts.name: Objection handling
concepts.summary: Identify likely reader objections about price, trust or effort and answer them with proof, guarantees or FAQs.

concepts.name: Unique value proposition
concepts.summary: Distinguish what makes an offer different from competitors and express it as a clear, specific claim.

concepts.name: Landing page copy architecture
concepts.summary: Arrange hero, benefits, proof, objections and CTA on a landing page so the message flows toward one action.

concepts.name: Tone and voice adaptation
concepts.summary: Adjust tone and formality to fit brand, audience and channel while keeping the message consistent.

concepts.name: Message-match across touchpoints
concepts.summary: Analyse whether an ad, email or link promise is carried through to the destination page, and fix mismatches.

misconceptions.text: Writers should invent the messaging from their own imagination rather than from customers' own words.
Using a framework like AIDA guarantees persuasive copy regardless of the audience.
Mentioning objections in copy plants doubts, so it is better to leave them out.

concepts.name: Psychological levers in persuasion
concepts.summary: Analyse how scarcity, social proof, authority, loss aversion and anchoring work in copy and where they backfire.

concepts.name: Ethical persuasion limits
concepts.summary: Judge whether a claim or urgency device is truthful and legally and ethically defensible, and rewrite it if not.

concepts.name: Funnel-stage copy strategy
concepts.summary: Plan how copy differs across awareness, consideration, purchase and retention stages and how pieces connect.

concepts.name: Email sequence design
concepts.summary: Evaluate and shape multi-email sequences by pacing, purpose per message and segmentation.

concepts.name: Copy critique and editing
concepts.summary: Assess a draft against goal, audience and clarity, and cut or restructure it to raise its effectiveness.

concepts.name: Interpreting performance data
concepts.summary: Read click-through, conversion and engagement metrics to diagnose which part of the copy is failing.

concepts.name: Copy testing design
concepts.summary: Design and evaluate copy tests with a single variable, a clear metric and enough sample to judge whether a variant truly won.

misconceptions.text: A test variant that has a higher conversion rate after a few days has proven it is better.
Fake urgency and scarcity are harmless because they reliably raise conversions.
The same message works at every funnel stage if it is written well enough.

concepts.name: Messaging strategy architecture
concepts.summary: Create a coherent messaging system of positioning, pillars and proof that guides all copy across channels and teams.

concepts.name: Evidence-based optimisation programme
concepts.summary: Design a continuous programme that turns research and test results into prioritised hypotheses and compounding learnings.

concepts.name: Evaluating persuasion trade-offs
concepts.summary: Judge when aggressive response tactics harm trust, retention or brand and choose approaches that balance both.

concepts.name: Market sophistication and differentiation
concepts.summary: Assess how saturated a market's claims are and craft angles that stand out when audiences have heard every promise.

concepts.name: Cross-cultural and localised copy
concepts.summary: Evaluate and adapt messaging for different cultures and languages beyond literal translation.

concepts.name: Briefing and directing writers
concepts.summary: Produce briefs and feedback standards that let other writers deliver on-strategy copy and develop a consistent house style.

concepts.name: Original concept and angle creation
concepts.summary: Generate and select original campaign ideas and angles grounded in customer insight that hold across formats.

misconceptions.text: Test results from one page or audience can be applied unchanged to every other context.
Maximising immediate conversion rate is always the right goal for copy.
Translating copy word for word is enough to localise it for a new market.
